summary: The runtime capability gate is fail-closed for malformed current schemas and preserves the prior chart/provenance checks, but the legacy compatibility regression does not exercise the actual immutable ad52 Helm archive.
validation: python3 hack/test-release-chart-flow.py -v passed 11/11 tests, including the loaded compatibility suite.
bash -n hack/verify-chart-artifact.sh and Python byte-compilation passed.
The diff retains checksum, chart-source-revision, archive/source/CRD parity, Helm schema/security-negative, and default-render validation before capability gating.
blockers: Legacy compatibility packages a new archive from exported ad52 source instead of passing the immutable ad52 Helm archive through the verifier; historical tar members, metadata, or generated content can regress unnoticed.
next_action: Return to test to run verify-chart-artifact.sh against the captured immutable ad52 archive and its checksum (or add an exact-byte fixture with provenance), while retaining the source-tree predicate tests.

issues.title: Legacy regression does not verify the actual immutable ad52 archive
issues.details: hack/test-chart-verifier-compat.py::test_immutable_v0613_source_archive_passes_current_verifier calls export_revision(ad52) and package_and_verify(), creating a fresh chart with the current packager. It never supplies the historical immutable Helm .tgz/checksum, so archive-specific compatibility is untested.
